newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL stocks slip on blue-chip selling, secondaries up.
newsitem.headline: KL stocks slip on blue-chip selling, secondaries up.

text.p: Blue-chip shares opened higher but retreated soon after due to a lack of momentum from local investors, brokers and analysts said on Wednesday.
They said the recovery in the Dow Jones industrial average had initially prompted buying, which could not be sustained due to lack of any other strong trading factors.
At 0215 GMT, the blue-chip Composite Index was up just 0.17 of a point at 1,078.14, after hitting a high of 1,082.51. The second board index was up 1.75 points to 571.19.
The brokers said focus continued to be on stocks in the news or those driven by rumours.
"There seems to be a lack of interest. There is no strong momentum after the Dow recovered, but it is too early to tell," said Patrick Zecha, head of research at South Johor Securities.
He said there were few overseas orders being seen in the market and much of the volume was still expected to come from situational stocks.
MBf Capital, which was requoted on Tuesday after being rejected permission to negotiate takeover of Suria Capital, recovered slightly to trade at 4.44 ringgit, up 22 cents.
Suria was up two cents at 2.57 ringgit.
Among index heavyweights, Maybank was unchanged at 26.25, Telekom was up 10 cents at 11.80 and Tenaga steady at 12.00 ringgit. Tanjong was up 15 cents to 8.90 ringgit.
